procedural_history.originating_court: Court of Judicature for Rajasthan at Jaipur
procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and Order dated 27.02.2015 of the High Court
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The High Court allowed the appeals in S. B. Sales Tax Revision Petition No. 59 of 2006.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The Appellant appealed the High Court's Judgment and Order dated 27.02.2015 to the Supreme Court.

arguments.issue_text: Whether sales tax, once paid, can be reduced or refunded based on a private agreement between the assessee and oil companies.
appellant_arguments: The appellant (the assessee) claimed that the amount of tax paid should be reduced or refunded, implying that their private agreement with oil companies should be considered in the final tax assessment.
respondent_arguments: There is no provision under the Act to reduce or refund tax once it has been paid.
The assessee's arrangement with the oil companies is a private agreement and is not the concern of the sales tax department.
Cited the precedent of MRF Ltd. v. Collector of Central Excise, Madras to support their position.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: The provided text does not contain the binding legal rule of the case. It only includes factual background, procedural details, and case citations without stating the legal principle applied by the court.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The court found that the precedent cited by the respondent, MRF Ltd. v. Collector of Central Excise, Madras, was irrelevant to the present case. The court reasoned that the MRF Ltd. case was decided under the Excise Act, where the taxable event is the removal of goods from the factory gate. This is a fundamentally different legal basis from the current sales tax matter, making the precedent inapplicable.
legal_tests_applied: Distinguishing precedent: The court analyzed the legal basis of a case cited by the respondent and found it inapplicable because it arose from a different statute (Excise Act) with a different taxable event (removal of goods from a factory) than the sales tax issue in the present case.
